head: claude/telegram-status-decisions-commands
title: telegram: add /status and /decisions operator pull commands
body:
## Summary

Two operator-pull commands on the polled Telegram bot, from the ask of 2026-09-02: **`/status`** posts the manager update "with the checklist and everything", and **`/decisions`** surfaces every decision still waiting on the operator "so they can all pop up at once. In case I don't get them as they come in."

Tier-2 — a live service (`ict-telegram-bot.service`) gains command handlers. **No order path.** Read-only except the *existing* decision-submit route, which is reused unchanged rather than re-implemented.

## ⚠️ A GREEN HARNESS PROVES NONE OF THIS

**The done-condition is the operator typing each command and getting a correct reply.** Everything below is a harness: 146 tests over stubbed Telegram objects, a stubbed inbox, and a fake `git` runner. Not one of them has sent a Telegram message, and this session has dispatched nothing to the VM. The specific things a harness structurally cannot reach:

- whether `ict-telegram-bot.service` on the live VM actually registers the handlers after a restart (this needs a Tier-2 deploy that has not happened);
- whether Telegram delivers `/status` to the chat at all — a `/command` reaches only a bot something is POLLING, and that property is a fact about the running fleet, not about this diff;
- whether a real tap on a `/decisions` button round-trips, which the `wdec` branch already owns and which `OI-20260901-DECISION-ROUNDTRIP-...` is still open on;
- what the tree stamp reads on the VM. Locally it reads `unknown` (this branch carries commits `origin/main` does not — correct behaviour, and the reason that state exists), so **`behind_main` has never been observed on real infrastructure**, only constructed in tests.

Merged is not deployed and deployed is not observed. Please treat this as *landed_unproven* until the operator has typed both commands.

## What each command does

### `/status` — `src/runtime/manager_status.py` (new)

Renders `MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json` + `SESSIONS.json` in the binding order **checklist → recently done → next**, asserted by test rather than assumed.

**The 4096-char problem is real and measured.** Population: all 57 items in `docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json` at `main` `0b52157` — **123,033 characters of JSON, mean 2,158 and max 7,532 per item**. A single item can exceed the whole message budget. So the readout summarises and degrades in a stated ladder: *fits → spill to a second message → compact to ids → drop*, and **what it compacts and what it drops it says, with counts.**

Rendered against the real file today: **2 messages, `recently_done` compacted, zero rows missing.** That ladder is not decoration — rendering the optional sections in full dropped **both of them entirely** (37 lines), so the operator got the checklist and neither of the other two parts they asked for. The first draft did exactly that; the compaction step exists because of it.

**Tree provenance is stamped on every readout** — `synced` / `behind_main` / `unknown`, never collapsed. One mapping is worth flagging for review: a tree that *differs* from `origin/main` while being behind it by **zero** commits grades `unknown`, not `synced`. It carries commits `main` does not, so what of `main` it reflects cannot be established; grading it `synced` would assert currency nobody measured, and grading it `behind_main` would name a direction the code did not compute.

### `/decisions` — `src/runtime/telegram_decisions.py`

Reuses the **same** `render_decision_prompt` / `build_decision_keyboard` / `fetch_inbox` / `answerable_route` the periodic sweep uses. Two copies of the `callback_data` construction is how the 64-byte budget and the option key-digest scheme drift apart, so a test asserts the on-demand keyboard is `==` the sweep's for the same request.

- `awaitingOperator` and `awaitingCommit` are reported **separately, never pooled** — an `in_transit` question is unanswered but waits on a *committer*, and counting it as the operator's would put work on their plate that is not theirs. `awaitingCommit` prints even at zero.
- `awaitingOperator` is `not_submitted + unreadable` on the route's own definition, so the `unreadable` share is **broken out**: we cannot send a button for a question we could not grade, and "N waiting" beside fewer than N prompts would read as a broken command.
- **Zero waiting produces an explicit "nothing is waiting for you."** Silence is indistinguishable from a broken command.
- `writeGate.acceptsWrites: false` → the reply **says answering is closed and why**, and the questions are sent **without buttons** rather than offering taps that 503.
- `unanswerableOperatorEdges` are surfaced when non-empty.
- An unreadable inbox reports *we could not look*, **never** an empty one.

**The marker interaction — decided, stated, tested.** `/decisions` **neither reads nor writes** `work_decision_prompted.json`. Not reading is the entire point of the ask; not writing keeps the periodic sweep exactly as it was. Writing a marker would *suppress* the sweep for a question the operator pulled, so a failed on-demand send would leave it asked by nobody; removing markers would make the sweep re-ask everything.

The accepted consequence, stated rather than hidden: **a question pulled here may also arrive once from the sweep shortly after.** A duplicate *prompt* is recoverable and a suppressed one is not, and it cannot produce a duplicate *decision* — the route answers a second submission with 409. Both halves are pinned: the marker file is byte-identical across a `/decisions` call, and the sweep still delivers its own one-time prompt afterwards.

### Wiring — `src/bot/operator_commands.py` (new)

Both commands resolve `telegram_decisions.answerable_route()` — **never a hardcoded token and never `claude_route()`**, asserted by AST over the module so the check cannot be satisfied by deleting the comment that explains the trap. They ride whatever bot is genuinely polled and follow **MI-58** to ClaudeBot with no second migration.

A route that does not resolve logs a **WARNING naming that `could_not_look` state and still registers** — a silently absent command is indistinguishable from a broken one, which is the failure this whole change exists to prevent. A route resolving to a *different* bot than this process polls is reported as `answerable_elsewhere` rather than assumed away, since MI-58 is deliberately changing that.

**Authorization:** the repo is PUBLIC and the bot username is discoverable, so both commands gate on the bot's **existing** `is_authorised` (the same check `callback_handler` uses, passed in rather than re-derived — a second notion of authorised is one that can drift). An unrecognised chat gets a refusal, never a dump; the refusal is logged; and a test asserts the gate runs **before** any state is read.

## Coordination

▶️ START posted on #6927 before the first commit ([comment](https://github.com/benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights/issues/6927#issuecomment-5508233531)) — via the `board-post` relay, because `add_issue_comment` 403s from this session (the documented read-only-MCP write-scope boundary, not the transient drop). This PR is opened through `pr-opener.yml` for the same reason.

**MI-58 (`claude/claudebot-answerable`) is working in `src/bot/telegram_query_bot.py` too.** This change touches that file in two places only — one import, and one `install_operator_commands(...)` call in `main()`'s registration block, plus a `_COMMAND_SURFACE` constant. `callback_handler`, the `wdec` branch, and `answerable_route()`'s resolution are **untouched**, which is what lets MI-58's migration carry both commands for free. `_MENU_OPENERS` deliberately keeps meaning *the openers*, so the pre-existing "no stale command wall" assertion still tests its original claim instead of being widened.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — no data schema, model boundary, pipeline stage, public API, or inter-process contract changes. Two new read-only modules and two Telegram command handlers; the decision-submit contract is consumed unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_manager_status.py` (31) — the 4096 path on a fixture sized like the real checklist (57 items, real state mix, real max title length), **asserting the omission count is stated** and that every message is within the cap; the compaction ladder; the binding section order; `behind_main` reachable *and* rendered distinguishably from `unknown`; every declared tree state reachable; `unknown` never carrying a fabricated `behind_commits: 0`; unreadable ≠ absent ≠ empty; owner grading never coercing free prose into a session id (measured: 19 of 57 items carry no owner, 11 read `manager`, several carry prose).
- [x] `tests/test_telegram_decisions.py` (98, was 73) — `/decisions` with **zero, one and several** waiting; only `not_submitted` sent; the cap stated rather than silently truncating; the two populations never pooled; closed/unknown write gate; unanswerable edges; unreadable and absent inboxes; the three tree caveats; **the marker interaction, both halves**; and the on-demand keyboard being `==` the sweep's.
- [x] `tests/test_operator_commands.py` (17) — refusal for an unrecognised chat on both commands, logged, with **no state read**; the injected predicate being the only decider; registration in all three route states; the adapter never constructing a `callback_data`.
- [x] `tests/test_telegram_query_bot.py` + `test_menu.py` — 37 passed, unchanged behaviour.
- [x] `scripts/ci/run_guards.py` — **49 passed, 0 failed** against the committed diff. Includes `collapsed-state-guard` with the new `manager_status.tree_state` contract, whose consumer is real (a stale tree is exactly what made the decisions route misgrade), not a branch added to satisfy the guard. `lint-imports`: 6 contracts kept, 0 broken.
- [ ] **CI green** — pending.
- [ ] **THE ONLY DONE-CONDITION: the operator types `/status` and `/decisions` and gets a correct reply.** Needs the Tier-2 deploy + an `ict-telegram-bot.service` restart. The manager will run that with them.

## Filed for follow-ups

- **Free-text decisions still cannot be answered from Telegram.** Inline buttons cannot carry arbitrary text. Such a request is still *sent* (so a blocking question is not invisible) and says plainly it needs the dashboard or the repo; the two populations are counted separately. Unchanged from the sweep — not a regression, and deliberately not half-built here.
- **`/decisions` sends at most 10 prompts per invocation**, with the remainder counted and named. A flood is the desensitised-alarm P1; if the real inbox routinely exceeds 10, the cap is the thing to revisit, not the message count.
- **No `/status` for the work store itself** (`/api/bot/work`) — this reads the manager checklist, which is what the operator asked for. A work-store view is Phase B's.
- Observed while reading, not fixed here: **3 of the 4 `blocked` checklist items declare no `blocked_on` edge.** `/status` reports that as `⚠️ blocked_on NOT DECLARED` rather than rendering them as ordinary blocked rows, which is how it surfaced. That is checklist data, not code.
